passages.text: When I heal Israel, the iniquity of Ephraim will be exposed, as well as the crimes of Samaria. For they practice deceit and thieves break in; bandits raid in the streets.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about Israel.
God says, "When I heal Israel, I will expose the sin of Ephraim."
I will also reveal the evil deeds of Samaria.
Ephraim and Samaria practice lies.
Thieves break into houses.
Bandits attack people in the streets.
passages.original: כְּרָפְאִ֣י לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וְנִגְלָ֞ה עֲוֺ֤ן אֶפְרַ֙יִם֙ וְרָע֣וֹת שֹֽׁמְר֔וֹן כִּ֥י פָעֲל֖וּ שָׁ֑קֶר וְגַנָּ֣ב יָב֔וֹא פָּשַׁ֥ט גְּד֖וּד בַּחֽוּץ׃

passages.text: But they fail to consider in their hearts that I remember all their evil. Now their deeds are all around them; they are before My face.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
God remembers all their evil.
The people do not think about this in their hearts.
God sees all their deeds.
Their deeds surround them now.
Their deeds are in front of God.
passages.original: וּבַל־ יֹֽאמְרוּ֙ לִלְבָבָ֔ם כָּל־ רָעָתָ֖ם זָכָ֑רְתִּי עַתָּה֙ סְבָב֣וּם מַֽעַלְלֵיהֶ֔ם נֶ֥גֶד פָּנַ֖י הָיֽוּ׃

passages.text: They delight the king with their evil, and the princes with their lies.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel do evil things.
Their evil actions make the king happy.
They tell lies.
Their lies please the princes.

passages.text: They are all adulterers, like an oven heated by a baker who needs not stoke the fire from the kneading to the rising of the dough.
passages.sermon:
The people are all adulterers.
They act unfaithfully.
They are like an oven.
A baker heats this oven.
The baker does not need to stir the fire.
He leaves the fire alone from the time he kneads the dough.
He waits until the dough rises.
The fire stays hot the whole time.
passages.original: כֻּלָּם֙ מְנָ֣אֲפִ֔ים כְּמ֣וֹ תַנּ֔וּר בֹּעֵ֖רָה מֵֽאֹפֶ֑ה יִשְׁבּ֣וֹת מֵעִ֔יר מִלּ֥וּשׁ בָּצֵ֖ק עַד־ חֻמְצָתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: The princes are inflamed with wine on the day of our king; so he joins hands with those who mock him.
passages.sermon: The princes become drunk with wine.\r\nThis happens on the day of our king.\r\nThe king joins hands with those who mock him.
passages.original: י֣וֹם מַלְכֵּ֔נוּ הֶחֱל֥וּ שָׂרִ֖ים חֲמַ֣ת מִיָּ֑יִן מָשַׁ֥ךְ יָד֖וֹ אֶת־ לֹצְצִֽים׃

passages.text: For they prepare their heart like an oven while they lie in wait; all night their anger smolders; in the morning it blazes like a flaming fire.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel have hearts full of evil desire.
Their hearts burn like an oven.
They plan to do wrong while they wait in secret.
Their anger does not rest.
Their anger smolders all night, like hot coals.
In the morning, their anger bursts out.
Their anger blazes like a flaming fire.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ קֵרְב֧וּ כַתַּנּ֛וּר לִבָּ֖ם בְּאָרְבָּ֑ם כָּל־ הַלַּ֙יְלָה֙ יָשֵׁ֣ן אֹֽפֵהֶ֔ם בֹּ֕קֶר ה֥וּא בֹעֵ֖ר כְּאֵ֥שׁ לֶהָבָֽה׃

passages.text: All of them are hot as an oven, and they devour their rulers. All their kings fall; not one of them calls upon Me.
passages.sermon:
The people are passionate and burning with desire, like a hot oven.
They destroy their rulers.
All their kings fall down.
None of them calls to God.
passages.original: כֻּלָּ֤ם יֵחַ֙מּוּ֙ כַּתַּנּ֔וּר וְאָכְל֖וּ אֶת־ שֹֽׁפְטֵיהֶ֑ם כָּל־ מַלְכֵיהֶ֣ם נָפָ֔לוּ אֵין־ קֹרֵ֥א בָהֶ֖ם אֵלָֽי׃

passages.text: Ephraim mixes with the nations; Ephraim is an unturned cake.
passages.sermon:
Ephraim is a tribe in Israel.
Ephraim mixes with other nations.
Ephraim does not remain separate.
Ephraim is like a cake not turned over.
Ephraim is not fully prepared.
Ephraim is incomplete and lacking.
passages.original: אֶפְרַ֕יִם בָּעַמִּ֖ים ה֣וּא יִתְבּוֹלָ֑ל אֶפְרַ֛יִם הָיָ֥ה עֻגָ֖ה בְּלִ֥י הֲפוּכָֽה׃

passages.text: Foreigners consume his strength, but he does not notice. Even his hair is streaked with gray, but he does not know.
passages.sermon:
Ephraim is a tribe in Israel.
Foreigners take away Ephraim’s strength.
Ephraim does not notice this loss.
Gray hairs appear on Ephraim’s head.
Ephraim does not realize this change.
passages.original: אָכְל֤וּ זָרִים֙ כֹּח֔וֹ וְה֖וּא לֹ֣א יָדָ֑ע גַּם־ שֵׂיבָה֙ זָ֣רְקָה בּ֔וֹ וְה֖וּא לֹ֥א יָדָֽע׃

passages.text: Israel’s arrogance testifies against them, yet they do not return to the LORD their God; despite all this, they do not seek Him.
passages.sermon:
Israel is proud.
Their pride stands before them.
This pride shows their guilt.
They do not return to the LORD their God.
They do not seek God.
They refuse to seek Him, even after all these things.
passages.original: וְעָנָ֥ה גְאֽוֹן־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּפָנָ֑יו וְלֹֽא־ שָׁ֙בוּ֙ אֶל־ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיהֶ֔ם וְלֹ֥א בִקְשֻׁ֖הוּ בְּכָל־ זֹֽאת׃

passages.text: So Ephraim has become like a silly, senseless dove— calling out to Egypt, then turning to Assyria.
passages.sermon:
Ephraim is a tribe in Israel.
Ephraim acts like a dove.
This dove is silly and has no sense.
Ephraim calls out to Egypt for help.
Ephraim goes to Assyria for help.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י אֶפְרַ֔יִם כְּיוֹנָ֥ה פוֹתָ֖ה אֵ֣ין לֵ֑ב מִצְרַ֥יִם קָרָ֖אוּ אַשּׁ֥וּר הָלָֽכוּ׃

passages.text: As they go, I will spread My net over them; I will bring them down like birds of the air. I will chastise them when I hear them flocking together.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about the people of Israel.
God says, "As they go, I will spread my net over them."
I will catch them in my net.
I will bring them down like birds from the sky.
I will punish them when I hear them gathering together.
passages.original: כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יֵלֵ֗כוּ אֶפְר֤וֹשׂ עֲלֵיהֶם֙ רִשְׁתִּ֔י כְּע֥וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם אֽוֹרִידֵ֑ם אַיְסִרֵ֕ם כְּשֵׁ֖מַע לַעֲדָתָֽם׃ס

passages.text: Woe to them, for they have strayed from Me! Destruction to them, for they have rebelled against Me! Though I would redeem them, they speak lies against Me.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about the people of Ephraim.
They have strayed away from God.
Woe comes to them because they left God.
Destruction comes to them because they rebelled against God.
God is willing to redeem them.
But they speak lies against God.
passages.original: א֤וֹי לָהֶם֙ כִּֽי־ נָדְד֣וּ מִמֶּ֔נִּי שֹׁ֥ד לָהֶ֖ם כִּֽי־ פָ֣שְׁעוּ בִ֑י וְאָנֹכִ֣י אֶפְדֵּ֔ם וְהֵ֕מָּה דִּבְּר֥וּ עָלַ֖י כְּזָבִֽים׃

passages.text: They do not cry out to Me from their hearts when they wail upon their beds. They slash themselves for grain and new wine, but turn away from Me.
passages.sermon:
The people do not cry out to God from their hearts.
They wail on their beds.
They hurt themselves for grain.
They hurt themselves for new wine.
They turn away from God.
passages.original: וְלֹֽא־ זָעֲק֤וּ אֵלַי֙ בְּלִבָּ֔ם כִּ֥י יְיֵלִ֖ילוּ עַל־ מִשְׁכְּבוֹתָ֑ם עַל־ דָּגָ֧ן וְתִיר֛וֹשׁ יִתְגּוֹרָ֖רוּ יָס֥וּרוּ בִֽי׃

passages.text: Although I trained and strengthened their arms, they plot evil against Me.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Israel.
God trained Israel.
God strengthened Israel’s arms.
Israel plots evil against God.
passages.original: וַאֲנִ֣י יִסַּ֔רְתִּי חִזַּ֖קְתִּי זְרֽוֹעֹתָ֑ם וְאֵלַ֖י יְחַשְּׁבוּ־ רָֽע׃

passages.text: They turn, but not to the Most High; they are like a faulty bow. Their leaders will fall by the sword for the cursing of their tongue; for this they will be ridiculed in the land of Egypt.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel turn away from God.
They do not return to the Most High.
They act like a faulty bow that cannot shoot straight.
Their leaders will fall by the sword.
Their leaders will die because of the evil words they speak.
People in Egypt will mock them.
Others will ridicule them because of their actions.
passages.original: יָשׁ֣וּבוּ׀ לֹ֣א עָ֗ל הָיוּ֙ כְּקֶ֣שֶׁת רְמִיָּ֔ה יִפְּל֥וּ בַחֶ֛רֶב שָׂרֵיהֶ֖ם מִזַּ֣עַם לְשׁוֹנָ֑ם ז֥וֹ לַעְגָּ֖ם בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
